q: Club Brugge were the first Belgian club to reach a European Cup final, in 1978. Who beat them, and at which ground?
KV Mechelen won the 1988 Cup Winners' Cup, still the last European trophy won by a Belgian club. Which Dutchman was their coach?
The Netherlands women won Euro 2017 on home soil. Which country did they beat 4-2 in the final?
The highest scoring match in Eredivisie history ended 9-5 in 1960. Which two clubs played it?
a: Feyenoord and Ajax, with Feyenoord winning

q: The biggest win in Eredivisie history is Ajax 12-1 in 1971-72. Who were the victims?
In October 2007 Afonso Alves scored seven goals in one Eredivisie match for Heerenveen. Who were the opponents, beaten 9-0?
Which Dutch coach took Trinidad and Tobago to their only World Cup, in 2006?
PEC Zwolle won the 2014 KNVB Cup, their first trophy in 104 years. What was the score in the final against Ajax?
Tilburg's club renamed itself Willem II in 1898. Who was he?
a: King William II of the Netherlands, who was based in Tilburg and died there

q: SC Telstar were founded in 1963 and named after what?
NAC Breda got their name from a 1912 merger. Which two clubs joined up?
Sparta are the oldest professional club in the Netherlands, but which Haarlem club, founded in 1879, is the oldest club of any kind?
Shirt sponsors were allowed in Dutch football from 1982. Which Japanese cassette tape brand sat on Ajax's shirt until 1991?
In 2020 the KNVB blocked FC Emmen's half a million euro main sponsor on grounds of decency. What did the company sell?
In February 2002 Roda JC won 1-0 away at which Italian giant, and still went out of the UEFA Cup?
a: AC Milan, on penalties at the San Siro

q: Sander Boschker won his only Netherlands cap in 2010, a record for the Dutch team. How old was he?
For thirty years people assumed Johan Cruyff skipped the 1978 World Cup over politics. What did he reveal in 2008 was the real reason?
a: A kidnap attempt on his family in Barcelona, with a gun held to his head

q: Belgium played the first official international between two independent countries in continental Europe, in 1904. Who were the opponents?
In the 1970s Belgium briefly switched to all white shirts for evening matches, and got a new nickname. What were they called?
In 1982 a Belgian club paid Waterschei to lie down in the title decider, a scandal that broke two years later. Which club?
In August 2015 ADO Den Haag's goalkeeper equalised against PSV in the 95th minute with a leaping backheel. Who was he?
Bjorn Kuipers refereed the Euro 2020 final. What was his day job back in Oldenzaal?
Roda JC fans call the team De Koempels. What does that word mean?
a: Mining mates, from the Kerkrade coal pits

q: In January 2010 a 121 year old club became the first Dutch professional side to go bankrupt in mid season. Which club?
Which Dutch coach snapped at a journalist with a line that entered the Dutch language, 'Am I so smart, or are you so stupid?'
Belgian clubs each carry a matricule, a registration number by seniority. Which club is number 1?
Racing Genk were created in 1988 by merging two clubs from the Limburg coalfield. Name either of them.
Which Kerkrade born coach, who gave his name to a skills training method, won the 1974 UEFA Cup with Feyenoord?
Fed up with the amateur KNVB, ten clubs set up a rebel professional league in 1954. The first match, on 14 August, drew 13,000 people. Which two clubs played it?
The Netherlands' first paid football club was founded in Geleen in June 1954 by a building contractor. What was it called?
After the 1953 flood disaster, a scratch team of Dutch professionals playing abroad went to Paris and beat France 2-1 for the victims. What did that match end up triggering back home?
Koninklijke HFC, the oldest club in the Netherlands, was founded in 1879 by Pim Mulier. How old was he at the time?
Belgium won Olympic gold in 1920 without finishing the final. Why did it stop after 39 minutes?
a: Czechoslovakia walked off in protest at the referee and were disqualified

q: The Netherlands took bronze at the 1920 Olympics, but only after losing the medal match itself. Who beat them to silver?
Anderlecht overturned a 2-0 deficit in the 1984 UEFA Cup semi-final, and admitted 13 years later they had paid the referee 27,000 pounds. Which English club did they knock out?
Standard's players bribed Waterschei to hand them the 1982 Belgian title. What was their stated motive for wanting an easy afternoon?
a: To avoid injuries before the Cup Winners' Cup final against Barcelona days later

q: KV Mechelen followed their 1988 Cup Winners' Cup with the European Super Cup. Which Dutch side, the reigning European champions, did they beat over two legs?
Which Nigerian scored the first ever goal in the rebranded Champions League, in November 1992, and for which club?
Two Brussels clubs, Racing White and Daring, merged in 1973 because nobody was turning up. What did the new club win two seasons later?
a: The Belgian title, in 1974-75, as RWD Molenbeek

q: A Belgian club took FIFA to court after their Moroccan midfielder Abdelmajid Oulmers was injured on international duty in 2004. Which club?
KAA Gent are nicknamed the Buffalos. Where does that come from?
a: Buffalo Bill's Wild West show visiting the city

q: In 2003 a Belgian club fielded a squad packed with graduates of an Ivorian academy, including Yaya Toure and Emmanuel Eboue. Which club?
Where exactly was RSC Anderlecht founded in May 1908?
a: In a cafe, the Concordia, in Anderlecht

q: Which Anderlecht great, known as the White Pele, lined up alongside Pele and Bobby Moore in the film Escape to Victory?
Before he was a cyclist, Remco Evenepoel was a midfielder at Anderlecht and PSV. What did he do for Belgium's under 16 side?
In 1975 a Rotterdammer at RWD Molenbeek became the first foreigner to win the Belgian Golden Shoe, and later won three straight titles coaching Anderlecht. Who?
In September 1965 Go Ahead hosted their first European tie in Deventer and lost 6-0. To whom?
The eagle on the Go Ahead Eagles badge has exactly seven feathers per wing. Why seven?
a: Because seven is a lucky number

q: Jan Jongbloed became the oldest man ever to play in the Eredivisie, aged 44, in 1985. Which club was he keeping goal for?
Rinus Michels took over a relegation threatened Ajax in January 1965. His first match finished 9-3. Who were the opponents?
MVV players are called De Sterrendragers, the star bearers. Where does the star come from?
a: The five pointed star in the coat of arms of Maastricht

q: MVV have played European football exactly once, winning their group in 1970. In which competition?
Joop van Daele's goal won Feyenoord the 1970 Intercontinental Cup against Estudiantes. What did the Argentines do to him seconds later?
a: Pulled off his glasses and snapped them in half

q: Ajax refused to play the 1973 Intercontinental Cup after their bruising 1972 meeting with Independiente. Which club took their place and lost?
PSV won the 1988 European Cup with a record nobody has matched. What was odd about their run?
a: They won only three matches in the whole campaign, and none from the quarter-finals onwards

q: De Kuip opened in 1937 with two free hanging tiers and no pillars. Which two stadiums were the models?
De Kuip nearly did not survive the Second World War. What did the German occupiers want to do with it?
NAC against Feyenoord in October 1979 was abandoned at 2-2 when a linesman was knocked down by a heavy glass ashtray. How were the last 27 minutes eventually played?
The first foreign professional in Dutch football arrived at Heracles in 1957 and was nicknamed the Black Meteor. Who was he?
Heracles Almelo had to change their spelling in 1906. What were they called when founded in 1903?
PEC in PEC Zwolle stands for a combination of two 1910 clubs, one named after a prince and one with a motto. What is that motto?
Dennis Bergkamp's father named him after Denis Law, but the name gained a letter. Why?
a: The Dutch registrar would not accept Denis, so his father added a second n

q: To prove he had the nerve to drop anyone, Louis van Gaal did something startling in the Bayern Munich dressing room. What?
In 1975 an amateur club from Spakenburg knocked out three professional sides and reached the KNVB Cup semi-final. Which club?
The fastest own goal in Eredivisie history came after nine seconds, in 2006-07. Which club's defender managed it?
The fastest goal in Eredivisie history took eight seconds. Koos Waslander did it in 1981-82 for which club?
The youngest goalscorer in Eredivisie history was 16 years and 100 days old in 1959-60. Which fishing town club did Wim Kras play for?
The fastest hat-trick in Eredivisie history took two minutes, scored by Jan Seelen in 1958-59. For which club?
Ruud Gullit was not born with that surname. What was he registered as?
Feyenoord's 1974 UEFA Cup win at De Kuip was wrecked by rioting in the away end. Which visiting manager took the stadium microphone to tell his own fans they were a disgrace?
